label: SYNTHETIC GOLD SET - questions written by the build agent, not by humans; not a benchmark

method.sampling: random.Random(42): shuffle the sorted indexed tickers, keep 13 (sorted); for each, sample 2 chunks (sorted by chunk_id) from Items 1A/7/7A with at least 900 characters. Reproduced by `scripts/eval_rag.py --show-sample`.
method.generator: Claude Opus 5.5 build agent, in-session (no API call), 2026-10-30, after reading the first 900 characters of each sampled chunk.
method.prompt: For each passage, write one natural question an investor might ask that this passage answers. Paraphrase: avoid copying distinctive phrases from the passage where a common synonym exists, do not name the company, keep it under 20 words.
caveats: Questions were written while reading the gold passage, so wording overlap is higher than for real user questions; this favors BM25.
Gold is a single chunk; neighbouring chunks share 15% overlap, so the lenient metric also accepts an adjacent chunk (same ticker and item, index +/-1).
Single annotator, no adjudication, 26 questions: differences of a few points are noise.

questions.question: What drove growth in AWS sales, and what partly offset it?
Has the company suffered security incidents before, and can its safeguards fully prevent data loss?
How might investor pressure over climate strategy and carbon frameworks affect access to capital?
Could the company be held liable for environmental damage even if it did not cause it?
Which European and US data protection laws apply to the company's activities?
How is adding AI features to search expected to influence revenue and margins?
What risks arise from transactions with governments or sovereign entities?
What are the principal legal and regulatory risk factors summarized by the bank?
How could the OECD global minimum tax and profit reallocation proposals affect the company?
When is a previously reserved uncertain tax benefit recognized in the accounts?
What risks come from bugs or reliability problems in the company's AI and software products?
What ethical or societal problems could arise from how customers use the company's AI?
How could net neutrality or network access fee rules affect the streaming business?
What happens if the company cannot protect its trademarks and domain names?
What are the consequences if personal data held by the company is stolen or misused?
How could an economic downturn hurt the company through its suppliers and customers?
Why are counterfeit medicines a risk for the company?
How does the company estimate the fair value of intangible assets in acquisitions?
How do online shopping and discount retailers change the competitive landscape?
Why does management treat productivity improvement as strategic?
What happens if CMS cuts Medicare Advantage benchmarks or changes risk adjustment payments?
How much liquidity does the company hold in cash and investment securities?
How do alternative payment systems such as real-time and P2P payments threaten the network?
How do movements in the euro affect results through the European subsidiary?
How do new lower-emission businesses like carbon capture and hydrogen depend on government policy?
Why are operating efficiency and cost control important to competitive performance?
